semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL clause 'This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected' names three distinct activating events. The exact transition inventory (transition:line:38, InitialState->ActiveState, trigger 'Collision Detected') is the sole entry into ActiveState, and the three named events are instead sourced from Inactive to dead-end leaves, so as literally stated the three-trigger activation obligation is not realized by any exact transition into ActiveState. A competent alternative reading is that 'sub-machine'/'active mode' refers loosely to ActiveState as a whole and 'Collision Detected' is an abstract merge of the three named causes; this reading is compatible with the same exact facts (same states/transitions), so it survives as an undercutting alternative even though the dossier itself calls it weak, since it does not contradict the exact bound facts, it only reinterprets them.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: NL2's 'sub-machine'/'active mode' may be read as referring to the single ActiveState composite as a whole, with the existing generic 'Collision Detected' trigger on InitialState->ActiveState treated as an abstraction over the three named collision-detection causes, so the single existing entry edge could be argued to satisfy the activation obligation under a generous event-merging reading.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: NL2 requires that the collision-avoidance sub-machine's active mode be entered upon any of Frontend_Collision_Detected, Rear_End_Collision_Detected, or Pedestrian_Collision_Detected; the exact closed-model transition inventory shows the only edge into ActiveState is InitialState->ActiveState triggered by the distinct 'Collision Detected' event, and the three named events instead fire only inside ActiveState (from Inactive to dead-end leaves), not as entry triggers into the active mode from outside.

response.reason: This lens compares the seven supplied atomic contracts against the exact closed FCSTM inventory, source inventory, and working-contract mapping to locate structural/contrastive defects: the top-level region cardinality, the collision-avoidance sub-machine activation entry, the guard-disjointness of the three activation alternatives, the orthogonal-region structure of ActiveState, the per-region default-entry structure, and the containment relation between the sub-machine and its active mode. Key finding: the closed FCSTM never models a separate 'collision-avoidance sub-machine' distinct from ActiveState itself -- ActiveState IS the ActiveState/active-mode composite that becomes active on InitialState->ActiveState (event Collision_Detected), not on any of the three collision-detection events (Frontend_Collision_Detected, Rear_End_Collision_Detected, Pedestrian_Collision_Detected). Those three events instead fire only after ActiveState is already active and Inactive is entered, driving transitions from Inactive to the three collision leaf states, which are dead-ends. This produces a wrong-trigger / missing-initial-entry structural mismatch for NL2's contract, and the guard-disjointness contract's three named collision events are not co-located transitions from a single shared source into an activation state at all - they are alternatives of a different existing group (Inactive -> FrontendCollision/RearEndCollision/PedestrianCollision), so their group-level disjointness must be assessed on the actual transitions. The three per-region initial-entry edges ([*]->BrakingControl etc.) are exact and satisfied within their own owner scope but the owning composites (FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion) are themselves unreachable from ActiveState's default entry (ActiveState's own initial edge goes only to Inactive, never into the three regions), which is a distinct root/owner reachability property from the per-region local edges. Also inspected working_contract/source_trace for macro protection status: FrontendCollisionRegion/RearEndCollisionRegion/PedestrianCollisionRegion are source-owned states (positively traced), not compiler-owned macro members, so the unreachable-region defects are genuine author-source-visible structural defects, not compiler artifacts.

result.reason: This lens compares the seven supplied atomic contracts against the exact closed FCSTM inventory, source inventory, and working-contract mapping to locate structural/contrastive defects: the top-level region cardinality, the collision-avoidance sub-machine activation entry, the guard-disjointness of the three activation alternatives, the orthogonal-region structure of ActiveState, the per-region default-entry structure, and the containment relation between the sub-machine and its active mode. Key finding: the closed FCSTM never models a separate 'collision-avoidance sub-machine' distinct from ActiveState itself -- ActiveState IS the ActiveState/active-mode composite that becomes active on InitialState->ActiveState (event Collision_Detected), not on any of the three collision-detection events (Frontend_Collision_Detected, Rear_End_Collision_Detected, Pedestrian_Collision_Detected). Those three events instead fire only after ActiveState is already active and Inactive is entered, driving transitions from Inactive to the three collision leaf states, which are dead-ends. This produces a wrong-trigger / missing-initial-entry structural mismatch for NL2's contract, and the guard-disjointness contract's three named collision events are not co-located transitions from a single shared source into an activation state at all - they are alternatives of a different existing group (Inactive -> FrontendCollision/RearEndCollision/PedestrianCollision), so their group-level disjointness must be assessed on the actual transitions. The three per-region initial-entry edges ([*]->BrakingControl etc.) are exact and satisfied within their own owner scope but the owning composites (FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion) are themselves unreachable from ActiveState's default entry (ActiveState's own initial edge goes only to Inactive, never into the three regions), which is a distinct root/owner reachability property from the per-region local edges. Also inspected working_contract/source_trace for macro protection status: FrontendCollisionRegion/RearEndCollisionRegion/PedestrianCollisionRegion are source-owned states (positively traced), not compiler-owned macro members, so the unreachable-region defects are genuine author-source-visible structural defects, not compiler artifacts.

branches.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability of the collision-avoidance regions, reachable event-consumer coverage for Collision_Avoided, dead-end frontier facts for the three collision leaf states, and the initial-entry/activation obligation for the sub-machine. Deterministic facts show that ActiveState is reachable from root and its Inactive default entry works (S2 satisfied for NL-CONTRACT-REF-002 at the ActiveState/Inactive owner scope), but the three orthogonal region composites (FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion) and their child controls (BrakingControl, SteeringControl, EmergencyStop) are structurally present (satisfying NL-CONTRACT-REF-004 region_structure and the region cardinality in NL-CONTRACT-REF-007) but are entirely unreachable from the top-level initial entry per inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL / refuted reachability checks). This produces a derived root-reachability defect for the active-mode's orthogonal regions, distinct from the region_structure declaration contract. Additionally, the reachable leaf states FrontendCollision/RearEndCollision/PedestrianCollision have no outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING, refuted deadlock checks), which is a deterministic V1 deadlock-frontier fact bearing on the state_action/progress obligation in NL-CONTRACT-REF-005 since those states are entered as the direct behavioral response to collision events but their required collision-avoidance controls (in the orthogonal regions) can never fire because the parent regions are unreachable — the concurrent activation of collision avoidance controls described in NL3 cannot occur.
